newsitem.title: USA: Action "very soon" on USDA vacancies-Glickman.
newsitem.headline: Action "very soon" on USDA vacancies-Glickman.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said Tuesday he hoped to see action "very soon" to fill high-level vacancies at the Agriculture Department.
"I have given suggestions to the White House on some of the positions," Glickman told Reuters. "I think we ought to be hearing very soon on some of the presidential nominations."
Four of the six undersecretary slots at USDA must be filled as well as the post of Farm Service Agency chief.
Senate Agriculture Committee chairman Richard Lugar (R-Ind.) said he has not been given any indication when nominees would be named or who they would be. Lugar promised speedy hearings on them.
Some private analysts, based on the lack of obvious action on the posts, have speculated the jobs will go to USDA officials.
"Wait and see. That's the best I can tell you," Glickman said when asked about that theory.
Lugar noted in an interview that the administration had been slow to fill USDA jobs in President Clinton's first term.
